Completed higher secondary education with Physics, Chemistry, and Mathematics.

projects.title: Campus Connect
projects.description: Task board for college students. Post a task, pick one up, and build a reputation as tasks get done. Changes appear for everyone in real time.
projects.problem: Students who need help with an assignment, an event or a project ask in scattered group chats, and nobody can see who took what or who usually delivers.
projects.solution: A React and Vite app on Firebase. Firebase Auth handles sign-up, and Firestore stores tasks and profiles, so a change reaches every open screen at once. Each profile keeps a helpfulnessScore and a tasksCompleted count that grow as tasks are finished.
projects.learnings: Shaping data around Firestore's real-time listeners, and turning Firebase error codes into messages people understand.
projects.future: Planned: a mobile app and calendar sync for task deadlines.

projects.title: FinAI (Hackfest 2025, IIT Dhanbad)
projects.description: Portfolio tracker with an ML risk model, built in 36 hours at Hackfest 2025, IIT Dhanbad. It prices holdings live from Yahoo Finance and gives each stock a risk score.
projects.problem: Beginner investors see prices but not risk. Judging a stock means reading beta, volatility and drawdown separately, and most people never do.
projects.solution: Three parts: a Next.js dashboard, an Express and MongoDB API that stores holdings and fetches live quotes in parallel, and a Flask service running a scikit-learn model. The model combines beta, 20-day volatility and drawdown into one risk bucket, and suggests similar stocks from a similarity matrix.
projects.learnings: Running the model as its own Flask service let the web work and the ML work move in parallel during a 36-hour build. Falling back to the stored price when a quote fails kept the dashboard usable.
projects.future: Planned: importing holdings from a broker, and alerts when a stock moves to a different risk bucket.

projects.title: Blogity
projects.description: Blogging platform where writers sign in and publish posts with images, and readers can subscribe to a newsletter.
projects.problem: Writers wanted a clean place to publish without setting up and maintaining a full CMS.
projects.solution: A Next.js app with NextAuth sign-in, posts and categories in PostgreSQL through Prisma, image uploads through UploadThing, and newsletter sign-ups sent to Beehiiv from an API route. A post and its author load in one Prisma query.
projects.learnings: Using Next.js route handlers as the whole backend, and keeping a 404 for a missing post separate from real server errors.
projects.future: Planned: markdown support, scheduled publishing and comment notifications.

projects.title: SkillSync
projects.description: Frontend prototype of a teammate finder for hackathons. Search people by skill, open their profile and message them.
projects.problem: Hackathon teams form in group chats, so finding someone with the one skill your team is missing is slow and mostly luck.
projects.solution: A Next.js and TypeScript frontend built with shadcn/ui on Radix: sign-up with a skills picker, a search that filters people by skill as you type, profiles and a chat screen. It runs on sample data; the matching API and real-time chat come next.
projects.learnings: Designing the screens first showed what the backend needs to store: a list of skills on each profile and conversations keyed by user. Also building accessible forms and dialogs on Radix primitives.
projects.future: Next: a backend for profiles and matching, real-time chat over WebSockets, and GitHub sign-in to import skills.

projects.title: GDG Recruitment Platform
projects.description: Recruitment system for GDG on Campus HIT. Applicants apply through one form, recruiters track every application, and admins promote the people they select to team members.
projects.problem: GDG on Campus HIT recruits from hundreds of applicants. Applications lived in forms and spreadsheets, so keeping track of who was reviewed, shortlisted or selected took a lot of manual work.
projects.solution: A Next.js app with NextAuth sign-in and PostgreSQL through Prisma. Applicants and members are separate tables. Promoting an applicant checks for an existing member with the same email, then creates the member with role, department and join date in one step.
projects.learnings: Modelling the workflow as data: keeping applicants and members apart turned promotion into one step that can be checked. Also how NextAuth sessions and Prisma fit together inside route handlers.
projects.future: Planned: stats for each recruitment round, bulk emails to applicants, and resume screening.

projects.title: Eshop
projects.description: Microservices e-commerce backend in an Nx monorepo, in early development. An API gateway sits in front of the services, starting with authentication.
projects.problem: I wanted to learn how a store splits into services (auth, catalogue, orders, payments) and what the gateway in front of them has to handle.
projects.solution: An Nx workspace with an Express API gateway and an auth service, a Dockerfile, and CI on GitHub Actions. The gateway allows only the storefront origin, rate-limits each IP (100 requests per 15 minutes), logs requests, and forwards them to the services behind it.
projects.learnings: Putting rules every service needs (CORS, rate limits, request logging) in the gateway once, instead of repeating them in each service.
projects.future: Next: sign-up and sign-in in the auth service, then catalogue, cart and order services, and the storefront shown in the concept mock-up.

features.title: API gateway
features.detail: One entry point with CORS and request logging

features.title: Service proxy
features.detail: Requests forwarded to the services behind it

steps.text: The storefront sends a request to the gateway with its cookies.
CORS accepts only the storefront origin, with credentials.
The rate limiter counts requests per IP and answers 429 over the limit.
express-http-proxy forwards the request to the service behind the gateway.
The service answers, and the gateway passes its response back.
